templates.description: Reads the pre-aggregated trips_monthly rollup from the sample-trips Postgres datasource for one calendar year: one row per (month, pickup zone) with trip count, revenue and tips. Expects an INTEGER parameter named year; the bounds are derived in Postgres (make_date) so the door is the year, never two dates. The shipped sample covers 2023 and 2024.
templates.body:
SELECT
    m.month_start     AS month_start,
    m.pu_location_id  AS pu_location_id,
    m.trip_count      AS trip_count,
    m.total_revenue   AS total_revenue,
    m.total_tips      AS total_tips
FROM trips_monthly m
WHERE m.month_start >= make_date(:year, 1, 1)
  AND m.month_start <  make_date(:year + 1, 1, 1)

templates.description: Reads the pre-aggregated trips_daily rollup from the sample-trips Postgres datasource for one calendar year: one row per day with trip count, revenue and distance. Expects an INTEGER parameter named year; the bounds are derived in Postgres (make_date). The shipped sample covers 2023 and 2024.
templates.body:
SELECT
    d.pickup_date       AS pickup_date,
    d.trip_count        AS trip_count,
    d.total_revenue     AS total_revenue,
    d.total_distance_mi AS total_distance_mi
FROM trips_daily d
WHERE d.pickup_date >= make_date(:year, 1, 1)
  AND d.pickup_date <  make_date(:year + 1, 1, 1)

templates.description: Reads the 265-row zone lookup from the sample-reference SQLite datasource. Takes no parameters. The two catch-all zones ('Unknown' and 'N/A') are excluded so a borough rollup has no bucket that is not a borough.
templates.body:
SELECT
    z.location_id  AS location_id,
    z.borough      AS borough,
    z.zone         AS zone_name,
    z.service_zone AS service_zone
FROM zones z
WHERE z.borough NOT IN ('Unknown', 'N/A')

templates.display_name: Weekend and US federal holiday calendar
templates.description: Reads the whole generated day calendar (731 rows, 2023-01-01..2024-12-31) from the sample-reference SQLite datasource: one row per day with the weekend and holiday flags. Takes no parameters - it is a lookup, and the answer node's join to the trips' days is what narrows it to the window. cal_date is ISO-8601 TEXT because SQLite has no DATE type; cast it after staging.
templates.body:
SELECT
    c.cal_date     AS cal_date,
    c.is_weekend   AS is_weekend,
    c.is_holiday   AS is_holiday,
    c.holiday_name AS holiday_name
FROM calendar c

templates.display_name: Daily precipitation across the NYC stations
templates.description: Averages the PRCP element across the five NYC-area GHCN stations, one row per day, from the sample-weather MySQL datasource, for one calendar year. Expects an INTEGER parameter named year; the bounds are derived in MySQL (MAKEDATE). Values are millimetres.
templates.body:
SELECT
    o.obs_date                AS obs_date,
    ROUND(AVG(o.value), 2)    AS precip_mm,
    ROUND(MAX(o.value), 2)    AS max_precip_mm
FROM observations o
WHERE o.element = 'PRCP'
  AND o.obs_date >= MAKEDATE(:year, 1)
  AND o.obs_date <  MAKEDATE(:year + 1, 1)
GROUP BY o.obs_date

templates.display_name: Join staged trips to staged zones, roll up by borough
templates.description: Runs in tempdb (H2) over stg_trips_monthly (Postgres) and stg_zones (SQLite). This is the cross-datasource join: neither engine can see the other's table, so both are staged first. Takes no parameters of its own.
templates.body:
SELECT
    z.borough                                                AS borough,
    SUM(t.trip_count)                                        AS trip_count,
    ROUND(SUM(t.total_revenue), 2)                           AS total_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(t.total_tips), 2)                              AS total_tips,
    ROUND(SUM(t.total_revenue) / SUM(t.trip_count), 2)       AS revenue_per_trip,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(t.total_tips) / SUM(t.total_revenue), 2) AS tip_pct_of_revenue
FROM stg_trips_monthly t
JOIN stg_zones z ON z.location_id = t.pu_location_id
GROUP BY z.borough
ORDER BY SUM(t.total_revenue) DESC

templates.display_name: Compare ridership on rainy versus dry days, by day type
templates.description: Runs in tempdb (H2) over stg_trips_daily (Postgres), stg_daily_rain (MySQL) and stg_calendar (SQLite) — a three-datasource join. Expects a BIGDECIMAL parameter named rain_threshold_mm; a day at or above it counts as rainy. Days with no weather observation count as dry.
templates.body:
SELECT
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(r.precip_mm, 0) >= :rain_threshold_mm THEN 'rainy' ELSE 'dry' END AS weather,
    CASE WHEN c.is_holiday = 1 THEN 'holiday'
         WHEN c.is_weekend = 1 THEN 'weekend'
         ELSE 'workday' END                                   AS day_type,
    COUNT(*)                                                  AS days,
    SUM(t.trip_count)                                         AS trip_count,
    ROUND(AVG(CAST(t.trip_count AS DECIMAL(18,2))), 1)        AS avg_trips_per_day,
    ROUND(SUM(t.total_revenue), 2)                            AS total_revenue
FROM stg_trips_daily t
JOIN stg_calendar c ON CAST(c.cal_date AS DATE) = t.pickup_date
LEFT JOIN stg_daily_rain r ON r.obs_date = t.pickup_date
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2

templates.description: Library template: per_unit(total, qty[, scale]) and share_pct(part, whole). Both guard the divisor with NULLIF, so an empty bucket yields NULL rather than failing the whole node. Imported by the H2 rollup templates under nyc/mobility/. Takes no parameters - a library never renders on its own.
templates.body:
<#-- nyc/lib/metrics.sql v1 - the two ratio shapes every borough rollup needs.
     Library: macro definitions only, no top-level output (templates.md 6.2). -->
<#macro per_unit total qty scale=2>ROUND(CAST(${total} AS DECIMAL(18,4)) / NULLIF(${qty}, 0), ${scale})</#macro>
<#macro share_pct part whole>ROUND(100.0 * CAST(${part} AS DECIMAL(18,4)) / NULLIF(${whole}, 0), 1)</#macro>

templates.display_name: Trips by pickup zone, drop-off zone and rate code
templates.description: Trip-level scan of the sample-trips Postgres database, rolled up to one row per (pickup zone, drop-off zone, rate code) for the window. This is the shared origin-destination staging source: the zone and rate-code lookups that turn these ids into boroughs, airports and fare bases live in a different engine, which is what makes the join a cross-engine one. The raw TLC feed carries implausible rows - the sample holds a trip recorded at 331,688 miles and 91,033 at zero distance - so this node keeps only 0 < distance < 100 miles and 0 < total < 1000 USD, which is 98.1 percent of the trips and is what makes an average a fact rather than an artifact of one bad row. Expects INTEGER parameters year and quarter (1-4); the quarter's bounds are derived in Postgres (make_date plus three months), so the door is the quarter the question names, never two dates. The shipped sample covers 2023 and 2024; one quarter keeps the trip-level scan at a few seconds.
templates.body:
SELECT
    t.pu_location_id                  AS pu_location_id,
    t.do_location_id                  AS do_location_id,
    t.rate_code_id                    AS rate_code_id,
    COUNT(*)                          AS trip_count,
    ROUND(SUM(t.total_amount), 2)     AS total_amount,
    ROUND(SUM(t.tolls_amount), 2)     AS total_tolls,
    ROUND(SUM(t.trip_distance_mi), 2) AS total_distance_mi
FROM trips t
WHERE t.pickup_date >= make_date(:year, 3 * :quarter - 2, 1)
  AND t.pickup_date <  (make_date(:year, 3 * :quarter - 2, 1) + INTERVAL '3 months')::date
  AND t.trip_distance_mi > 0 AND t.trip_distance_mi < 100
  AND t.total_amount     > 0 AND t.total_amount     < 1000
GROUP BY t.pu_location_id, t.do_location_id, t.rate_code_id

templates.description: Reads the seven-row rate-code lookup from the sample-reference SQLite datasource - the fare basis a trip was metered on (Standard rate, the JFK flat fare, Newark, Nassau or Westchester, Negotiated fare, Group ride, Unknown). Takes no parameters.
templates.body:
SELECT
    r.rate_code_id AS rate_code_id,
    r.description  AS rate_code
FROM rate_codes r

templates.description: Trip-level scan of the sample-trips Postgres database at (day, pickup zone) grain - the grain a weather join needs, which neither shipped rollup has. The raw TLC feed carries implausible rows - the sample holds a trip recorded at 331,688 miles and 91,033 at zero distance - so this node keeps only 0 < distance < 100 miles and 0 < total < 1000 USD, which is 98.1 percent of the trips and is what makes an average a fact rather than an artifact of one bad row. Expects INTEGER parameters year and quarter (1-4); the quarter's bounds are derived in Postgres (make_date plus three months). The shipped sample covers 2023 and 2024; one quarter keeps the trip-level scan at a few seconds.
templates.body:
SELECT
    t.pickup_date                 AS pickup_date,
    t.pu_location_id              AS pu_location_id,
    COUNT(*)                      AS trip_count,
    ROUND(SUM(t.total_amount), 2) AS total_amount
FROM trips t
WHERE t.pickup_date >= make_date(:year, 3 * :quarter - 2, 1)
  AND t.pickup_date <  (make_date(:year, 3 * :quarter - 2, 1) + INTERVAL '3 months')::date
  AND t.trip_distance_mi > 0 AND t.trip_distance_mi < 100
  AND t.total_amount     > 0 AND t.total_amount     < 1000
GROUP BY t.pickup_date, t.pu_location_id

templates.display_name: Daily weather elements, averaged across stations
templates.description: One row per day from the sample-weather MySQL database, with precipitation, snowfall, maximum temperature and wind speed pivoted into columns and averaged across the five NYC-area stations. Expects INTEGER parameters year and quarter (1-4); the quarter's bounds are derived in MySQL (MAKEDATE plus three months). Values: millimetres, degrees Celsius, metres per second.
templates.body:
SELECT
    o.obs_date                                                   AS obs_date,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN o.element = 'PRCP' THEN o.value END), 2) AS precip_mm,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN o.element = 'SNOW' THEN o.value END), 2) AS snow_mm,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN o.element = 'TMAX' THEN o.value END), 1) AS tmax_c,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN o.element = 'AWND' THEN o.value END), 1) AS wind_ms
FROM observations o
WHERE o.obs_date >= MAKEDATE(:year, 1) + INTERVAL (3 * :quarter - 3) MONTH
  AND o.obs_date <  MAKEDATE(:year, 1) + INTERVAL (3 * :quarter) MONTH
  AND o.element IN ('PRCP', 'SNOW', 'TMAX', 'AWND')
GROUP BY o.obs_date

templates.description: Reduces the staged origin-destination pairs to one baseline row per PICKUP borough - the denominator the airport comparison is read against. It is derived from the SAME staged table as the numerator on purpose: a baseline taken from the monthly rollup instead would also count trips whose drop-off zone has no borough, and the resulting share would have a denominator its numerator was never drawn from. Reads only staged tables; takes no parameters of its own.
templates.body:
SELECT
    z.borough                                                          AS borough,
    SUM(o.trip_count)                                                  AS borough_trip_count,
    <@met.per_unit total="SUM(o.total_amount)" qty="SUM(o.trip_count)"/> AS borough_revenue_per_trip
FROM stg_od_pairs o
JOIN stg_zones z ON z.location_id = o.pu_location_id
GROUP BY z.borough

templates.description: The answer node of airport_access_by_borough. Joins the staged origin-destination pairs to the staged zone lookup TWICE - once for the pickup end, once for the drop-off end - keeps only legs whose drop-off zone is an airport, labels them with the staged rate-code lookup - so the share metered on an airport FLAT fare (the JFK and Newark rate codes) rather than the standard meter is an exact count, not a guess at which label sorts last - and reads each borough's airport economics against its own baseline. Reads only staged tables.
templates.body:
SELECT
    pu.borough                                                              AS pickup_borough,
    dz.zone_name                                                            AS airport,
    SUM(o.trip_count)                                                       AS airport_trips,
    <@met.per_unit total="SUM(o.total_amount)" qty="SUM(o.trip_count)"/>       AS revenue_per_trip,
    <@met.per_unit total="SUM(o.total_distance_mi)" qty="SUM(o.trip_count)"/>  AS miles_per_trip,
    <@met.per_unit total="SUM(o.total_tolls)" qty="SUM(o.trip_count)"/>        AS tolls_per_trip,
    MAX(b.borough_revenue_per_trip)                                          AS borough_revenue_per_trip,
    <@met.share_pct part="SUM(o.trip_count)" whole="MAX(b.borough_trip_count)"/> AS pct_of_borough_trips,
    SUM(CASE WHEN rc.rate_code IN ('JFK', 'Newark') THEN o.trip_count ELSE 0 END) AS flat_fare_trips,
    <@met.share_pct part="SUM(CASE WHEN rc.rate_code IN ('JFK', 'Newark') THEN o.trip_count ELSE 0 END)" whole="SUM(o.trip_count)"/> AS pct_flat_fare
FROM stg_od_pairs o
JOIN stg_zones pu ON pu.location_id = o.pu_location_id
JOIN stg_zones dz ON dz.location_id = o.do_location_id
LEFT JOIN stg_borough_baseline b ON b.borough = pu.borough
LEFT JOIN stg_rate_codes rc ON rc.rate_code_id = o.rate_code_id
WHERE dz.service_zone IN ('Airports', 'EWR')
GROUP BY pu.borough, dz.zone_name
ORDER BY SUM(o.trip_count) DESC

templates.description: The answer node of borough_od_matrix. Resolves both ends of every staged origin-destination pair through the staged zone lookup and rolls the result up to a borough-by-borough matrix. Reads only staged tables; the pickup-borough filter is bound from the pipeline's borough parameter.
templates.body:
SELECT
    pu.borough                                                             AS pickup_borough,
    dz.borough                                                             AS dropoff_borough,
    SUM(o.trip_count)                                                      AS trip_count,
    ROUND(SUM(o.total_amount), 2)                                          AS total_amount,
    <@met.per_unit total="SUM(o.total_amount)" qty="SUM(o.trip_count)"/>      AS revenue_per_trip,
    <@met.per_unit total="SUM(o.total_distance_mi)" qty="SUM(o.trip_count)"/> AS miles_per_trip
FROM stg_od_pairs o
JOIN stg_zones pu ON pu.location_id = o.pu_location_id
JOIN stg_zones dz ON dz.location_id = o.do_location_id
WHERE :pickup_borough = 'All' OR pu.borough = :pickup_borough
GROUP BY pu.borough, dz.borough
ORDER BY pu.borough, SUM(o.trip_count) DESC

templates.display_name: Ridership by borough, weather and day type (tempdb)
templates.description: The answer node of weather_sensitivity_by_borough. Joins four staged tables from three source engines - daily trips by zone (Postgres), daily weather (MySQL), the zone lookup and the weekend/holiday calendar (SQLite) - and splits each borough's ridership by wet/dry and by day type. Grouped on ordinals because the wet/dry expression carries a bound parameter (templates.md 8.4).
templates.body:
SELECT
    z.borough                                                                            AS borough,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(w.precip_mm, 0) >= :rain_threshold_mm THEN 'wet' ELSE 'dry' END   AS weather,
    CASE WHEN c.is_holiday = 1 THEN 'holiday'
         WHEN c.is_weekend = 1 THEN 'weekend'
         ELSE 'workday' END                                                              AS day_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT d.pickup_date)                                                        AS days,
    SUM(d.trip_count)                                                                    AS trip_count,
    <@met.per_unit total="SUM(d.trip_count)" qty="COUNT(DISTINCT d.pickup_date)" scale=0/> AS trips_per_day,
    <@met.per_unit total="SUM(d.total_amount)" qty="SUM(d.trip_count)"/>                   AS revenue_per_trip
FROM stg_daily_by_zone d
JOIN stg_zones z    ON z.location_id = d.pu_location_id
JOIN stg_calendar c ON CAST(c.cal_date AS DATE) = d.pickup_date
LEFT JOIN stg_daily_weather w ON w.obs_date = d.pickup_date
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY 1, 2, 3

templates.display_name: Borough briefing over the composed matrix (tempdb)
templates.description: The answer node of mobility_briefing. Reads the borough-by-borough matrix produced by the CHILD pipeline (delivered into tempdb by the PIPELINE node) and reduces it to one line per borough: trips, the share that never leaves the borough, and revenue per trip. The first column binds :run_fiscal_quarter, the value the fiscal_quarter CALCULATOR node wrote into the execution Context, so the run labels itself. Every number comes from the one child result, so the numerator and the denominator are the same population.
templates.body:
SELECT
    :run_fiscal_quarter                                                    AS fiscal_quarter,
    o.pickup_borough                                                       AS borough,
    MAX(z.zone_count)                                                      AS pickup_zones,
    SUM(o.trip_count)                                                      AS trip_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.dropoff_borough = o.pickup_borough THEN o.trip_count ELSE 0 END) AS trips_within_borough,
    <@met.share_pct part="SUM(CASE WHEN o.dropoff_borough = o.pickup_borough THEN o.trip_count ELSE 0 END)" whole="SUM(o.trip_count)"/> AS pct_within_borough,
    <@met.per_unit total="SUM(o.total_amount)" qty="SUM(o.trip_count)"/>      AS revenue_per_trip
FROM stg_od_matrix o
LEFT JOIN (SELECT borough, COUNT(*) AS zone_count FROM stg_zones GROUP BY borough) z
       ON z.borough = o.pickup_borough
GROUP BY o.pickup_borough
ORDER BY SUM(o.trip_count) DESC

pipelines.name: nyc/mobility/revenue_by_borough
pipelines.description:
Question
Which NYC borough earns the most yellow-taxi revenue in a year, and which tips best. One row per pickup borough, ranked by revenue.

Window and door
One calendar year, chosen by the year parameter (default 2024). The templates derive the bounds in their own dialect; there is no start or end date to pass.

Sources and grain
sample-trips (Postgres): trips_monthly, one row per (month, pickup zone) - a rollup of a deterministic 1-in-16 hash sample of yellow-taxi trips, local New York dates, USD. sample-reference (SQLite): zones, the 265-row TLC zone lookup that maps a pickup zone id to its borough. Two engines, so both are staged into tempdb and joined there.

Interpretation
Trip counts are sample counts: multiply by 16 to estimate the population, and never read them as a share against a full-count feed. tip_pct_of_revenue is tips over total revenue (every trip, not card-paid trips only - the rollup has no payment split). The zone lookup's two catch-all rows ('Unknown', 'N/A') are excluded, so no bucket that is not a borough is ranked.

Verification
Source total for 2024, SELECT SUM(trip_count), SUM(total_revenue) FROM trips_monthly WHERE month_start >= '2024-01-01' AND month_start < '2025-01-01': 2,527,759 trips, 72,642,978.77 USD. The six rows sum to 2,518,747 trips and 72,264,742.61 USD; the difference (9,012 trips, 0.36%) is the trips whose pickup zone is a catch-all - the exclusion above, measured.

Caveats
EWR is the zone lookup's label for Newark Airport, not a borough; it appears as its own row. A year with no rows in the sample (anything but 2023 or 2024) returns zero rows, not an error.

year.description: The calendar year to report, as the question names it (2024). The sample covers 2023 and 2024.

nodes.description: Stage the year's monthly rollup from the sample-trips Postgres database: one row per (month, pickup zone).
Stage the taxi-zone lookup from the sample-reference SQLite database.
Join the two staged tables in tempdb and roll up by borough.

pipelines.name: nyc/mobility/rainy_vs_dry_ridership
pipelines.description:
Question
Do New Yorkers take more taxis when it rains? One row per (weather, day type): rainy or dry, crossed with holiday, weekend or workday - six rows, each with its days, trips and average trips per day.

Window and door
One calendar year, chosen by the year parameter (default 2024). The rainy threshold is the rain_threshold_mm parameter (default 2.5 mm). Both trip and weather templates derive the year's bounds in their own dialect.

Sources and grain
sample-trips (Postgres): trips_daily, one row per day - a 1-in-16 hash sample of yellow-taxi trips. sample-weather (MySQL): observations, GHCN daily elements for five NYC-area stations, averaged to one PRCP value per day in millimetres. sample-reference (SQLite): calendar, one row per day with weekend and holiday flags. Three engines, one answer, joined in tempdb on the day.

Interpretation
A day is rainy when the five stations' average precipitation is at or above rain_threshold_mm (2.5 mm is the US National Weather Service 'light rain' floor); a day with no PRCP reading counts as dry. Day type is holiday first, then weekend, else workday. Counts are sample counts (x16 for the population); the comparison of interest is the per-day AVERAGE, which the sample rate does not distort.

Verification
SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(trip_count) FROM trips_daily WHERE pickup_date >= '2024-01-01' AND pickup_date < '2025-01-01': 366 days, 2,527,759 trips - the six rows sum to exactly that. Rainy days from the weather source, SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT obs_date, AVG(value) p FROM observations WHERE element = 'PRCP' AND obs_date >= '2024-01-01' AND obs_date < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY obs_date) d WHERE p >= 2.5: 76, the same 76 the three rainy rows hold.

Caveats
Every 2024 day has a PRCP reading, so the 'no reading counts as dry' rule changed nothing in this window; it would on a year with gaps. The holiday flag is the calendar's - eleven US federal holidays - not a school or transit calendar.

year.description: The calendar year to report, as the question names it (2024). The sample covers 2023 and 2024.

rain_threshold_mm.description: Average daily precipitation, in millimetres, at or above which a day counts as rainy.

nodes.description: Stage the year's daily trip counts and revenue from the sample-trips Postgres database: one row per day.
Stage the year's daily precipitation from the sample-weather MySQL database: one row per day, averaged across the five stations.
Stage the whole weekend/holiday calendar from the sample-reference SQLite database: one row per day; the answer node's join narrows it to the window.
Join all three staged tables in tempdb and compare rainy against dry days.

pipelines.name: nyc/mobility/borough_od_matrix
pipelines.description:
Question
Where do the trips that start in each borough actually end up? One row per (pickup borough, drop-off borough) with trips, revenue, revenue per trip and miles per trip; filter to one pickup borough with pickup_borough.

Window and door
One calendar quarter, chosen by year and quarter (default 2024, 3: July to September). The trip-level template derives the quarter's bounds in Postgres; there is no start or end date to pass.

Sources and grain
sample-trips (Postgres): trips, trip-level rows of a 1-in-16 hash sample of yellow-taxi trips, local New York dates, USD - rolled up at the source to one row per (pickup zone, drop-off zone, rate code), about 4.9M rows a year down to a few thousand. sample-reference (SQLite): zones, the TLC zone lookup, joined at BOTH ends in tempdb.

Interpretation
The raw TLC feed carries implausible rows (the sample holds a trip recorded at 331,688 miles and 91,033 at zero distance), so the source template keeps only 0 < distance < 100 miles and 0 < total < 1000 USD; that is what makes miles_per_trip a fact rather than an artifact of one bad row. A pair is counted only when both ends resolve to a borough: the two catch-all zones are excluded from the lookup, so a trip with an unknown end is not in the matrix.

Verification
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_date >= '2024-07-01' AND pickup_date < '2024-10-01' AND trip_distance_mi > 0 AND trip_distance_mi < 100 AND total_amount > 0 AND total_amount < 1000: 583,112 trips (593,730 before the plausibility filter). The 27 rows sum to 577,205; the 5,907 short of the source are the trips with a catch-all zone at one end - the exclusion above, measured.

Caveats
EWR is the lookup's label for Newark Airport, not a borough; it appears as a pickup and a drop-off row of its own. Trip counts are sample counts (x16 for the population); the ratios are unaffected.

year.description: The calendar year to report, as the question names it (2024). The sample covers 2023 and 2024.

quarter.description: The calendar quarter of that year to report, 1-4 (the default, 3, is July to September).

pickup_borough.description: Restrict the matrix to one pickup borough - Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Bronx, Staten Island or EWR. The default 'All' matches every borough.

nodes.description: Stage the quarter's trips by pickup and drop-off zone from the sample-trips Postgres database: one row per (pickup zone, drop-off zone, rate code).
Stage the taxi-zone lookup from the sample-reference SQLite database.
Resolve both ends of every pair through the zone lookup and roll up borough by borough.

pipelines.name: nyc/mobility/airport_access_by_borough
pipelines.description:
Question
Which boroughs ride to JFK, LaGuardia and Newark, what does that trip cost, and how does it compare with the borough's ordinary economics? One row per (pickup borough, airport), ranked by trips.

Window and door
One calendar quarter, chosen by year and quarter (default 2024, 3: July to September). The trip-level template derives the quarter's bounds in Postgres.

Sources and grain
sample-trips (Postgres): trips, a 1-in-16 hash sample of yellow-taxi trips, rolled up at the source to one row per (pickup zone, drop-off zone, rate code). sample-reference (SQLite): zones (the TLC zone lookup, used at both ends of the journey) and rate_codes (the seven fare bases). Five nodes across the two engines: the rollup, the two lookups, a per-borough baseline computed in tempdb from the SAME staged rows as the numerator, and the answer node that reads one against the other.

Interpretation
An airport leg is a trip whose drop-off zone's service_zone is 'Airports' or 'EWR' - the lookup's own classification, not a zone-name match. pct_of_borough_trips is airport legs over the borough's plausibility-filtered trips in the same quarter, from the same staged table, so numerator and denominator are one population. flat_fare_trips counts legs metered on the JFK or Newark flat rate codes; pct_flat_fare is that over the airport legs. The plausibility filter (0 < miles < 100, 0 < total < 1000 USD) is applied at the source.

Verification
The JFK zone id is 132 in the lookup (SELECT location_id FROM zones WHERE zone = 'JFK Airport'); the Manhattan zone ids are the 69 rows WHERE borough = 'Manhattan'. Against the source: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trips WHERE do_location_id = 132 AND pu_location_id IN (<those 69 ids>) AND pickup_date >= '2024-07-01' AND pickup_date < '2024-10-01' AND <the plausibility filter>: 4,876 - exactly the Manhattan / JFK Airport row's airport_trips. Re-run it before releasing.

Caveats
Trip counts are sample counts (x16 for the population). A borough with no airport legs in the quarter has no row rather than a zero row. EWR as a PICKUP borough is Newark Airport's own zone, not a borough.

year.description: The calendar year to report, as the question names it (2024). The sample covers 2023 and 2024.

quarter.description: The calendar quarter of that year to report, 1-4 (the default, 3, is July to September).

nodes.description: Stage the quarter's trips by pickup and drop-off zone from the sample-trips Postgres database: one row per (pickup zone, drop-off zone, rate code).
Stage the taxi-zone lookup from the sample-reference SQLite database.
Stage the rate-code lookup from the sample-reference SQLite database.
Reduce the staged pairs to one baseline row per pickup borough, in tempdb.
Keep the airport-bound legs, label the fare basis, and read each borough against its own baseline.

pipelines.name: nyc/mobility/weather_sensitivity_by_borough
pipelines.description:
Question
Which boroughs lose riders when it rains, and which barely notice? One row per (borough, weather, day type) - wet or dry, crossed with holiday, weekend or workday - with days, trips, trips per day and revenue per trip.

Window and door
One calendar quarter, chosen by year and quarter (default 2024, 3: July to September). The wet threshold is rain_threshold_mm (default 2.5 mm). The trip and weather templates derive the quarter's bounds in their own dialect.

Sources and grain
sample-trips (Postgres): trips, a 1-in-16 hash sample, rolled up at the source to one row per (day, pickup zone). sample-weather (MySQL): observations, GHCN daily elements for five NYC-area stations, pivoted and averaged to one row per day (precipitation mm, snow mm, max temperature C, wind m/s). sample-reference (SQLite): zones and the whole calendar. Three source engines staged into one tempdb.

Interpretation
A day is wet when the five-station average precipitation is at or above rain_threshold_mm; no reading counts as dry. Day type is holiday, then weekend, else workday. trips_per_day divides the cell's trips by its own number of days, so a borough's wet and dry rows are comparable. The plausibility filter (0 < miles < 100, 0 < total < 1000 USD) is applied at the source; the two catch-all zones are excluded.

Verification
The quarter has 92 days (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM calendar WHERE cal_date BETWEEN '2024-07-01' AND '2024-09-30'); each of Bronx, Brooklyn, Manhattan and Queens sums to 92 days across its six rows. Wet days from the source, SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT obs_date, AVG(value) p FROM observations WHERE element = 'PRCP' AND obs_date >= '2024-07-01' AND obs_date < '2024-10-01' GROUP BY obs_date) d WHERE p >= 2.5: 21 - Manhattan's three wet rows sum to 21 days.

Caveats
EWR (Newark Airport's zone) and Staten Island have pickups on only 22 and 24 of the 92 days, so their per-day figures rest on thin bases. Trip counts are sample counts (x16 for the population).

year.description: The calendar year to report, as the question names it (2024). The sample covers 2023 and 2024.

quarter.description: The calendar quarter of that year to report, 1-4 (the default, 3, is July to September).

rain_threshold_mm.description: Average daily precipitation, in millimetres, at or above which a day counts as wet.

nodes.description: Stage the quarter's daily trips by pickup zone from the sample-trips Postgres database: one row per (day, pickup zone).
Stage the quarter's daily precipitation, snow, temperature and wind from the sample-weather MySQL database: one row per day.
Stage the taxi-zone lookup from the sample-reference SQLite database.
Stage the whole weekend/holiday calendar from the sample-reference SQLite database: one row per day; the answer node's join narrows it to the quarter.
Join all four staged tables in tempdb and split each borough by weather and day type.

pipelines.name: nyc/mobility/mobility_briefing
pipelines.description:
Question
The quarterly mobility brief: one line per borough - how many trips start there, how many never leave it, and what a trip is worth - for the last complete quarter.

Window and door
The last complete calendar quarter BEFORE anchor_date (default 2025-01-01, the day after the sample's last day, so the default briefs 2024-Q4). A CALCULATOR node (trailing_periods, one quarter back from the anchor) writes the window's first and last day into the execution Context; two more derive the window's calendar year and quarter, which the PIPELINE node maps into the child's year and quarter door - so the child is asked in its own vocabulary and no raw date is passed anywhere.

Sources and grain
Built by COMPOSITION: the first node runs borough_od_matrix as a real child execution, pinned to version 1, and stages its (pickup borough, drop-off borough) matrix into this pipeline's tempdb; sample-reference (SQLite) zones is staged to count each borough's pickup zones. Every number comes from that one child result, so the share and its denominator are the same population.

Interpretation
trips_within_borough are the child's rows whose drop-off borough equals the pickup borough; pct_within_borough is that over the borough's trips. The fiscal_quarter column labels the run with the quarter the window ends in under the deployment's own fiscal start (the org_fiscal_start_date key), so the same pipeline labels itself correctly on a deployment whose fiscal year does not start in January. The child's plausibility filter and catch-all exclusion apply.

Verification
The child's own cross-check applies to the window the anchor resolves: for the default, SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trips WHERE pickup_date >= '2024-10-01' AND pickup_date < '2025-01-01' AND trip_distance_mi > 0 AND trip_distance_mi < 100 AND total_amount > 0 AND total_amount < 1000 gives 669,779 trips; the six rows' trip_count sums to 663,500, and the 6,279 short of the source are the trips with a catch-all zone at either end (the child's exclusion, measured). Re-run it before releasing.

Caveats
An anchor inside a quarter briefs the quarter BEFORE it (2024-12-31 briefs 2024-Q3, 2025-01-01 briefs 2024-Q4) - that is what 'last complete quarter' means. EWR is Newark Airport's zone, not a borough. Trip counts are sample counts (x16 for the population).

anchor_date.description: The day the briefing is written: the brief covers the last complete calendar quarter BEFORE this date. The sample ends 2024-12-31, so the default (the day after the data's last day) briefs 2024-Q4; pass 2024-10-01 for 2024-Q3.

nodes.description: The last complete calendar quarter before the anchor: one CALCULATOR node (trailing_periods, one quarter back) writing the window's first and last day into the Context as window_start and window_end.
The calendar year of the window's first day, for the child's year door. fiscal_year with a January fiscal start IS the calendar year; the catalog has no bare calendar-year kind.
The calendar quarter (1-4) of the window's first day, for the child's quarter door.

Run the borough_od_matrix pipeline as a pinned child execution over the window's year and quarter - the child's own door, mapped from this pipeline's derived values - and stage its result: one row per (pickup borough, drop-off borough).
Stage the taxi-zone lookup so the briefing can count each borough's pickup zones.

Label the run with the fiscal quarter the window ends in. A CALCULATOR node: no SQL, no rows - one typed value written into the execution Context under run_fiscal_quarter, which the briefing node binds as :run_fiscal_quarter. fiscal_start comes from the deployment's own setting, so the same pipeline labels its output correctly on a deployment whose fiscal year does not start in January.
Reduce the child's matrix to one briefing line per borough, labelled with the window's fiscal quarter.
